market_holds: Spot $9.28 (sealed 18:10 UTC 11-10), +12.6% over 5 sessions and +34.9% over 20, about 40% off the ~$6.6 low of 10-21, still -74% from the 52-week high. The front (11-13) straddle reads 45% but the ATM spread is 69% of mid, so it is indicative only; the median of the last 7 print reactions is 8.7% (max +58% on 2026-08-14, when the call disclosed the upper-limb amendment path). The P&L does not matter (consensus loss -$0.61, Earnings Whispers preview 11-04); the stock trades on the deramiocel BLA, PDUFA 2026-11-22, which falls AFTER this window. That followed a 9-3 negative AdCom on cardiomyopathy (07-29) and a major amendment refocused on upper-limb function. The sell-side leans CRL: HC Wainwright expects a CRL (10-05), Roth floats a second panel, Koyfin has 4 of 10 at Buy. The short is crowded: Nasdaq short interest is 19.86M shares on 10-15, 6.6 days to cover, roughly a third of ~58M shares. Retail is bullish and reading job posts and the investigators' letter (dated 10-25) as tea leaves. Rough arithmetic: cash of about $3.5/share against an approval value in the mid-$20s puts implied approval odds near 25%.
view: This print is a regulatory-tone event 12 days before a binary PDUFA, not an earnings event. The only thing in tonight's release or call that can move the open is what management says about the FDA review: labeling discussions, the status of the July BIMO Form 483, any late-stage communication, or a sign that the FDA wants another panel. Management has a record of sharing positive process milestones, and has done so by standalone release (mid-cycle completion PR'd 2025-05-05; CEO in June 2026 said labeling talks would turn 'serious' within weeks). But no 8-K has been filed since 2026-08-24. Two and a half months with no process news from a talkative company, plus a physician lobbying letter to FDA leadership, lean mildly toward a review that is not going smoothly. Against that, the stock is heavily shorted, retail is bullish, and any constructive phrase ('labeling discussions', '483 closed') could squeeze a short of about a third of the shares into the open. The more likely release ('active review, on track for Nov 22') leaves the run-up to fade a little or sit. The distribution is skewed: a likely modest dip, a less likely large gap up. The straddle and the stock's own crowding already price that shape. I cannot see which branch the release lands in, so there is no edge.

recommendation.reason: The window turns on whether management signals that FDA labeling talks are underway. That is close to a proxy for the PDUFA outcome, which public information does not reveal and which the stock (about 25% implied approval odds) and a ~45% straddle already price as a binary. The weak negative tea leaves (no process 8-K since August, the lobbying letter, the sell-side leaning CRL) are offset by a crowded short and the stock's habit of rising on its calls (5 of 7). No mechanism is left that the price lacks.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Explicit language in the release or call that labeling or post-marketing commitment discussions with CBER have begun, or that the Form 483 was closed. That would make long the right side with a large gap. Conversely, a statement that the FDA has requested another advisory committee, or management declining to discuss the review at all, would make short right.

self_critique: The skew argument may underplay the up side. Management controls the release, is talkative, faces a short of about a third of the shares, and has an incentive to show confidence twelve days out. Even vague wording ('active, collaborative labeling-stage dialogue') could gap the stock 15-30% at the open, as in August. On the other side, if the FDA has already signalled problems, careful post-litigation disclosure could produce a flat or evasive call, and the 40% bounce since 10-21 could give back 10-15%. Neither branch can be seen from public data, so 47 stands.
